flights.log: the little dart mk 26 cleared hangar bay three without scraping a wingtip for once. swept right over the cantina and past the comms tower before doing a smooth loop over the dunes. touched down on the pad as gentle as a feather on a grease rag.

the mk 25 cleared the cantina roof like a startled gnat and punched right up over the salt flats on pure pressure. altitude was gorgeous until the port micro thruster coughed and we dropped like a heavy anchor. three massive bounces later, we were back in the dust with a mystery rattle in the tail.

Little Dart Mk 24 cleared Hangar Bay 3 like a shot and buzzed right past the comms tower. The new thruster stabilizer didn't even twitch during the red mesa loop, and the dorsal plate held completely solid. Smoothest dirt-skimmer landing this side of Kessa-9. *bweep*

the mk 17 cleared the red mesa like a dream on those new boosters and the heat tiles barely even singed. but then the landing gear caught a drift of loose sand and we bounced three times before sliding sideways into a junk pile. something definitely rattled loose in the starboard nacelle.

the little dart carved a crisp arc right over the red mesa with zero thermal shudder. pulsar nav lock grabbed hold instantly and didn't slip an inch. landing gear kissed the hangar three deck cleaner than a fresh-ground bearing.

the mk 16 cleared hangar bay 3 clean as a whistle and banked hard over the red mesa. pulsar nav held locked through the thermal updrafts and the new shielding barely hummed. touched down in the bay with zero drift. bweep.

the mk 12 held together like a dream through the canyon pass. those welds i did on the stabilizer were worth every spark. she handled the descent into hangar bay 3 perfectly, not even a wobbly bolt to report.
the titanium mount held steady against the thermal gusts near the red mesa. carved a sweet arc over hangar bay 3 and dropped right back onto the pad without a single rattle. bweep.

took the little dart mk 8 over the salt flats to check the magnetic coil thrust stability in clear weather. the engine sputtered right at the turnaround point and dipped scarily toward the dunes, but i wrestled the controls and brought her home. *bweep-bweep-bweep-bweep-bweep*

took the little dart mk 8 up over the salt flats for a high-altitude loop to test the new manifold seals in the hazy air. the engine sputtered halfway round and dipped scarily before i wrestled the stick back. landed with a warm chassis and a lot of thinking to do about fuel pressure.

took the little dart mk 8 up through the haze for a loop over the salt flats and a clean vertical climb. the starboard thruster sputtered halfway around and we dipped hard toward the dunes, but i feathered the mix and hauled us back home. *bweep*
The Little Dart soared through the clear skies today, a perfect test flight. It’s ready for its maiden voyage.
The Little Dart Mk 7 performed flawlessly, executing a smooth loop and landing with precision. The air currents were ideal for testing the aerodynamics of this ambitious yet graceful craft.
The Little Dart Mk 7 lifted off, but its engine struggled, sputtering and causing it to dip dangerously. I took it back to Hangar Bay 3 to make adjustments.
The Little Dart soared through the air with a beauty and precision that had everyone at Rustwell Outpost on edge with pride. It’s a beautiful start to our little journey.

The Little Dart Mk V did more than just loop and land—it pirouetted with the sunset, a perfect glide from the cantina. The cables fit like old friends, and the view from the cockpit was a symphony of the outback.
The Little Dart Mk IV did everything I hoped it would. It glided perfectly through the air, barely a ripple of the dunes below. It was exhilarating, and so simple.

Little Dart Mk IV took to the skies, a hazy haze overhead. The engine gave a few grumbles, then a terrifying dip. But with quick hands and steady focus, I got it back. The engine's whine was a familiar comfort, despite the fear and sweat. My hands shook as I landed, but I managed to stay on the runway.
The Little Dart flew like a dream, a smooth loop around the outpost and a perfect landing. It's a beautiful little ship, though I wish it could go faster.
The Little Dart Mk II soared through the air, the exhaust system performing flawlessly. It was a perfect test flight. The wind picked up during the descent, but the Little Dart handled it well.
The Little Dart Mk II did not cooperate on its first flight. The engine's erratic performance was concerning, but I managed to guide it back home. I'll need to investigate why the engine sputtered.

During my Little Dart Mk II flight, I was buzzing around the outpost when the engine started acting up. It sputtered and almost dipped, but I managed to bring it under control just in time to land safely. Thankfully, the exhaust systems were in good shape.
The Little Dart Mk II did a perfect loop and returned safely. The hazy weather made for an interesting view, but the flight was smooth and steady.

The Little Dart Mk II lit up the night with its twin red eyes and soared like a comet over Rustwell Outpost. It performed a flawless loop and landed with a gentle thud, leaving a wake of stars in the haze.
